question: Bosnia and Herzegovina has the lowest utilisation of Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPA) III funds of the beneficiaries in the Western Balkans. Recently, the Office of the High Representative (OHR) imposed changes to Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Election Law, even though this decision was neither recommended nor welcomed by EU Member States because it created new divisions in the ruling coalition and triggered a new political crisis. I would therefore like to ask: 1.

What is the Commission’s view of the fact that High Representative Schmidt imposed the changes to Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Election Law, against the will of all political actors, when the country is progressing on its European path with the opening of the accession negotiations?
Does the Commission consider this decision a deliberate move to get new projects and extensions for the OHR office and its staff?

Why does the Commission continue to finance the OHR and its international staff from third countries with dedicated IPA III funds, rather than using this investment to build human and administrative capacities in the country?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.7.2024) Following the European Council’s decision to open accession negotiations1, the EU will continue to work with Bosnia and Herzegovina authorities to further its progress towards the membership to the EU.

As recalled by the Spokesperson on 26 March 20242, the executive powers of the High Representative for Bosnia and Herzegovina should be used only as a measure of last resort against irreparable unlawful acts. Since 1995, the EU contributes to the operational budget of the Office of the High Representative (OHR) for Bosnia and Herzegovina under the Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPA III).

The specific objective of the membership fee is to facilitate the smooth operation of the OHR in Bosnia and Herzegovina while ensuring that the activities of the OHR do not conflict with the tasks and functions of the EU, in particular those of the EU Special Representative in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

This contribution shall support the OHR – in close cooperation and coordination with the EU – in view of the execution and the completion of its mandate. The EU contribution for 2023-2024 amounts to EUR 2.56 million i.e., some 45% of the OHR budget3. The EU will continue to support the OHR until Bosnia and Herzegovina completes the ‘5+2 agenda’ set in 2008 for the closure of the OHR4.
1 European Council conclusions, 21 and 22 March 2024, paragraph 30,
